Road Layer.Specific Description: The roadway was slightly curving to the right prior to the crash site. This curvature, while not severe, reduced visibility and potentially contributed to the driver of Vehicle #2 being unaware of Vehicle #1's stopped position in time to react.

The roadway had undivided lanes. The absence of a physical divider meant Vehicle #2 had a direct line of sight to Vehicle #1, but also meant there was no barrier to prevent the collision once the driverâs attention was diverted.

Object Interaction Layer.Specific Description: Vehicle #2 was following Vehicle #1 too closely. Vehicle #1 was stopped to allow traffic to pass, and Vehicle #2 impacted the rear of Vehicle #1, indicating insufficient following distance to react safely when Vehicle #1 decelerated to a stop.

There appears to have been a large longitudinal speed difference between Vehicle #1 and Vehicle #2. Vehicle #1 was stopped, while Vehicle #2 was traveling at a speed that the driver admitted was too fast to avoid the collision once the stopped vehicle was observed.

Vehicle #2 performed emergency braking, indicating a late reaction to Vehicle #1 being stopped. The driver attempted to brake but was unable to avoid the impact, confirming the limited time and distance available for a safe stop.

Environment Layer.Specific Description: The roadway was dry, so this is not a risk factor.

Other Relevant Risk Layer.Specific Description: The driver of Vehicle #2 was externally distracted by showing his girlfriend the trees. This distraction led to a delayed perception of Vehicle #1 being stopped, ultimately contributing to the rear-end collision. This is not contained in the restricted list.
